description: CMA-ES minimises a function of real variables by sampling λ points from a multivariate normal distribution `N(m, σ² C)`. After each generation it moves the mean `m` towards a weighted mean of the best points. It learns the covariance matrix `C` from successful steps, so the samples line up with the valleys of the function; it also adapts the global step size `σ` from the length of an averaged search path (*cumulative step-size adaptation*). The update uses only the ranks of the costs, so any strictly increasing transform of the cost gives the same run. Use it for non-convex, badly scaled or non-separable continuous problems with up to a few hundred variables; it is a local, stochastic method, and restarts with larger populations (IPOP) make it more global.
